examples.inference: Establishing pre-deployment data discovery and permission governance resolves risk committee bottlenecks, enabling rapid enterprise scaling.
examples.framing_bias: Vendor asserts that adopting pre-deployment controls leads to 40% faster scaling to promote its onboarding solutions.

examples.stated_factor: Internal technical migration labor and dual user training overhead
examples.statistic: $10.4M in internal labor/migration costs; 8 hours training per user; 12 IT FTEs over 6 months
examples.inference: The high financial cost of dual user training and dedicated technical migration labor represents substantial hidden deployment overhead that challenges ROI justification.
examples.framing_bias: TEI methodology sponsored by vendor documents training and IT FTE overhead primarily as financial line items rather than user friction or workflow disruption.

examples.stated_factor: Diffuse pilot deployments yielding only microproductivity gains
examples.inference: Fragmented, pilot-driven rollouts of generic assistants fail to deliver meaningful business value or ROI because organizations lack operating model strategy and end-to-end process integration.
examples.framing_bias: Consultancy contrasts 'microproductivity' with real financial return to steer clients away from ad-hoc tool adoption toward structured, high-fee consulting transformations.

examples.stated_factor: difficulty quantifying productivity gains and lack of leadership vision
examples.statistic: 59% of leaders worry about quantifying productivity gains; 60% worry leadership lacks a plan
examples.inference: Uncertainty in proving productivity ROI alongside absent executive roadmaps halts broader organizational rollout.
examples.framing_bias: Vendor attributes stalled copilot adoption to leadership lack of vision and measurement difficulties rather than software utility or pricing hurdles.

examples.stated_factor: Unsanctioned Shadow AI apps and high-risk third-party OAuth connectors
examples.statistic: 98% of companies have employees using shadow AI; avg 1,200 unofficial apps per company; 25% of unverified OAuth apps high-risk
examples.inference: Unvetted OAuth integrations and unmonitored Shadow AI applications create credential scope overprivilege and bypass enterprise access controls.
examples.framing_bias: Data security vendor Varonis highlights third-party OAuth app sprawl and shadow AI threats to sell SaaS security posture management.

examples.stated_factor: Shadow IT proliferation and compliance governance risks in large enterprises
examples.inference: Shadow IT proliferation bypasses enterprise security controls, breaks compliance policies, and prevents auditing of corporate data exposures.
examples.framing_bias: Analyst emphasizes shadow IT risks to promote enterprise-wide governance and vendor-sanctioned tooling suites.

examples.stated_factor: Absence of enterprise AI usage guidelines and insufficient employee training
examples.statistic: 68% never used AI at work; 37% lack company AI guidelines; only 15% strongly agree they have needed training
examples.inference: Organizations lack clear acceptable-use policies and formal training curricula, leaving employees hesitant, uncertain of permissions, and unequipped to utilize AI assistants effectively.
examples.framing_bias: Vendor frames lack of adoption as a corporate enablement and training deficit rather than questioning product-market fit or ROI clarity.

examples.stated_factor: formal enterprise adoption lag versus informal worker adoption
examples.statistic: only 5.4% of firms had formally adopted generative AI
examples.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
examples.inference: Discrepancy between grass-roots worker adoption and formal enterprise deployment stems from slow executive governance, compliance sign-offs, and risk policies.

examples.stated_factor: lack of EHR integration
examples.statistic: 84% cite EHR integration as required attribute
examples.inference: Lack of deep, real-time bidirectional integration with legacy and proprietary Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems directly impedes clinical AI deployment.

examples.stated_factor: friction from standalone tools vs. deep workflow embedding
examples.inference: Friction caused by standalone tools requires deep integration into core clinical EHR systems and restructuring of clinical operating workflows.
examples.framing_bias: Vendor frames workflow friction as an architectural best practice lesson, encouraging deeper platform lock-in.

examples.stated_factor: native EHR vendor platform integration
examples.statistic: 21.9 percentage points higher likelihood for Epic users
examples.inference: Native platform integration from dominant EHR vendors (e.g. Epic) removes technical systems access barriers, dramatically accelerating provider adoption.

examples.stated_factor: Improved written clarity and tone in drafted outputs and cognitive load reduction
examples.statistic: 73% reported improved outputs; 0.49 pt increase on 7-point scale
examples.publisher: UK Department for Work and Pensions (DWP)
examples.inference: High-quality draft generation improves communication clarity, tone, and reduces cognitive load, directly enhancing public sector knowledge worker output.

examples.stated_factor: Surging bulk power system complexity demanding augmented operator cognition and vigilance
examples.inference: Surging grid operational complexity and cognitive demands drive utilities to adopt AI copilot tools to enhance operator capacity and redesign control room workflows.
examples.framing_bias: Industry body frames grid complexity as an unavoidable operational pressure that forces adoption of assistive AI to maintain reliability.

examples.stated_factor: lack of agent guardrails, monitoring, and governance controls
examples.statistic: only 24% of organizations possess guardrails and live monitoring for agent actions
examples.inference: The absence of guardrails and monitoring indicates an inability to audit, log, and govern autonomous agent behaviors, preventing organizations from safely authorizing active agent operations.
examples.framing_bias: Cisco frames governance guardrails as an enterprise networking/monitoring infrastructure deficit to position its AI visibility and security platforms.

examples.stated_factor: regulatory compliance and mandatory pre-deployment data classification overhead
examples.statistic: 58% of UK FSI firms added controls; 43% increase in healthcare data classification
examples.inference: Heavily regulated sectors like financial services and healthcare must satisfy strict data privacy and compliance mandates before rolling out AI search tools.
examples.framing_bias: Vendor highlights regulatory friction to position pre-deployment data classification software as a compliance necessity.
